title: Strings Fundamentals

steps.title: A string is text
steps.content: A string is an ordered sequence of characters. In Python, strings are immutable: operations create a new string rather than changing one character in place.
steps.example: word = 'Bounty'; word[0] is 'B'. Indexing starts at 0.
steps.tip: For a string of length n, valid positive indices are 0 through n−1.

steps.title: Index a string
steps.explanation: C=0, O=1, D=2, I=3. The character at index 3 is I.

steps.title: Slice a substring
steps.content: Slicing uses text[start:end]. The start index is included and the end index is excluded. Negative indices count from the end.

steps.title: Predict a slice
steps.explanation: Indices 1,2,3 are Y,T,H. The end index 4 is excluded, so the result is YTH.

steps.title: Common string operations
steps.content: Useful operations include lower(), upper(), strip(), split(), join(), replace() and membership with 'in'. Be careful: split() returns a list, not a string.

steps.title: Trace a string slice
steps.content: A slice includes its start index and stops before its end index.
steps.explanation: Index 1 is 'o' and index 2 is 'd'. Index 3 is excluded, so the output is od.

questions.explanation: Index -1 refers to the final character.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Python strings is true?
questions.explanation: Python strings are immutable; operations return new strings.
split(',') divides the string into a list using comma as the separator.

learning_objectives: Explain strings as sequences of characters.

common_misconceptions.misconception: The last character is at index length.
common_misconceptions.correction: The last valid index is length - 1.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A slice always includes its end index.
common_misconceptions.correction: In Python-style slicing, the end index is excluded.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Changing one character always mutates the original string.
common_misconceptions.correction: Many languages use immutable strings; create a new string for changes.

worked_examples.title: Access a character
worked_examples.explanation: A string can be treated as an indexed sequence of characters.

worked_examples.title: Trace a slice
worked_examples.explanation: The end boundary is exclusive in Python slicing.

worked_examples.title: Count a traversal
worked_examples.explanation: A single pass over a string of length n takes O(n) time.

company_applications.practice: Trace indices and handle empty or one-character strings.
Practice substring boundaries and character counting.
Explain time complexity and test repeated characters.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Strings Fundamentals?
srs_cards.answer: Explain strings as sequences of characters. Access characters safely using indices. Trace slices and substring boundaries. Use common string operations. Recognize immutability differences across languages.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Strings Fundamentals.
srs_cards.answer: The last valid index is length - 1.
